messages:
jen_support: FYI - Acme (customer) opened a ticket: streaming chat replies constantly drop mid-response when they reconnect via their corporate gateway. Works intermittently in our hosted UI, but reproducible with their client behind the gateway.

jen_support: Customer report: initial stream starts, then after ~20-30s they see partial chunk, client reconnects with the same session token and gets a new short chunk, sometimes duplicated text fragments. They attached pcap + server logs. Billing concern: they were billed for the partial tokens and want credits.

alex: Can you paste the minimal reproduction command they used? h2 vs h1 reproduce?

jen_support: They used: ```curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  --http2 \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream?sess=abc123``` and then a variant with `--no-http2`.

jen_support: With --http2 they get truncation ~20s in. With --no-http2 (forces h1) the stream stays stable. Customer's gateway logs show many `RST_STREAM` and `PROTOCOL_ERROR` entries when token rotation occurs.

alex: Do we have the request-id or trace ids from the server logs? Need to correlate with gateway entries.

jen_support: Yes - server trace id: trace=tr-0971b2. Attached snippet from our proxy logs: ```[2026-03-10T16:12:03Z] trace=tr-0971b2 client=10.4.2.8 : : method=POST path=/v1/chat/stream status=200 bytes=1200 duration=24s stream_closed_by=client reason=RST_STREAM code=11```

dmitri: Looks like the intermediate gateway is doing HTTP/2 connection reuse and performing token rotation mid-connection. If an auth proxy reauthorizes the TCP connection and rewrites `:authority` or some headers, the h2 muxed streams can get torn down. gRPC-gateways sometimes translate to h1 upstream causing chunk boundary changes.

chris: We saw similar before: some proxies buffer/merge SSE chunks when translating between h2<>h1. That can produce partial events on reconnect. Workarounds: 1) disable h2 on client or 2) include a stable per-stream header (x-stream-id) so reconnects create a new logical stream server-side, or 3) set `Connection: close` to avoid connection reuse (not great for perf).

oncall-bot: deploy-canary: Rolling canary to staging with small runtime fix (tune: reject mid-connection auth rotations) started by dmitri at 2026-03-10T16:30:00Z :rocket:

dmitri: Quick repro steps for eng: 1) run h2 proxy that does token refresh/rotation (we have a local python stub) 2) client `curl --http2 -N` to server behind proxy 3) force proxy to rotate auth header mid-stream. Expected: RST_STREAM + truncated event.

dmitri: Example proxy (minimal) to flip header: ```# python proxy_stub.py
# on connect: forward stream
# after 25s: replace Authorization header and issue SETTINGS frame / push
``` (high level). I added the stub to the incident doc.

alex: Can you attach the customer's pcap or at least the h2 frame dump? h2 frame boundaries will show RST_STREAM or CONTINUATION fragmentation.

jen_support: Attached h2dump: ```[h2dump] stream 27: HEADERS -> 200
[h2dump] stream 27: DATA (len=512) END_STREAM?=0
[h2dump] stream 27: RST_STREAM (0x1) error=0x1b``` They reported many CONTINUATION frames with 0-length data around reconnect.

chris: That RST_STREAM error code 0x1b maps to PROTOCOL_ERROR in some proxies. When proxies attempt to inject headers mid-connection without proper continuation semantics it triggers reset.

jen_support: Customer also sees duplicate fragments after reconnect (server-side emitted same tokens twice). They suspect the client replay logic on reconnect isn't deduping.

alex: For immediate mitigation: suggest customer switch their client to `--no-http2` or set their gateway to not rotate tokens on live connections. Also offer billing credit request - I'll approve up to 1 day of token usage while we investigate.

jen_support: I'll propose the credit and ask for their confirmation. They want a fix on our side if we can do anything to tolerate proxy behaviour.

dmitri: Long-term fixes we discussed: 1) mark event-streams with `x-allow-mid-connect-refresh: true` and implement server logic to treat mid-connection reauth as a no-op for active streams; 2) emit a unique stream id header and make reconnects idempotent at application layer (server dedupe); 3) detect RST_STREAM with PROTOCOL_ERROR from upstream and log as a distinct metric to detect problematic gateways.

chris: Also consider documenting known proxy incompatibilities (gRPC gateways that rewrite headers, corporate TLS-terminating middleboxes) and recommended client configs.

alex: Please add the server-side trace lines (trace=tr-0971b2) to the escalation ticket and link the pcap. I'll route to eng-runtime + infra.

jen_support: Done. Linking ticket: INC-2026-4237. Customer accepted temporary credit. Keeping this thread updated with canary results. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary: staging runtime patch deployed to 10% of hosts at 2026-03-10T16:34:22Z - monitor: stream-reset-rate metric.

alex: Thanks team. If canary reduces RST_STREAM rate we can schedule a full rollout. Otherwise we'll need to implement application-layer dedupe.

jen_support: Noted. Will follow up after canary window (30m).
